one_month_reasoning: Inside Oct 2-31: (1) Nebius list-price increases took effect Oct 1 (B300 on-demand +21% to $9.50/hr, H100 +17%), largely priced after the Sep 17 move; the Oct 1 Inferize acquisition is small. (2) Hyperscaler Q3 reports in the last week of October, where 2027 capex guides drive neocloud sentiment; raises are more likely than cuts but tone and leasing commentary matter. (3) The 10Y at 5.29% after a +33bp week and possible residual ATM supply are mild headwinds. Nebius Q3 results have no announced date (company events page); Q1/Q2 were reported May 13/Aug 12, so mid-November is most likely, with perhaps ~15% chance of an in-window report. No strong edge: lognormal around $232.28 with monthly sigma 28% (106%/3.5 = 30%, trimmed for compressed recent vol) and a -0.5% drift for rates/supply. Round 4 (site inventory, split discounting) changes long-run value only; no site energization, contract or financing event is scheduled inside Oct 2-31 (the AIB lease was signed Sep 30 and is small), so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of a site-mapped capacity-vintage DCF ($121 at Oct-2027 with split discounting: signed investment-grade contract cash flows at 8.5%, signed unrated Q2-26 deals at 10.5%, everything else and the terminal at WACC 12.3%; $118 at one WACC) and EV/NTM EBITDA ($275: 9x on $12.1B, 400M shares). The DCF spans ~$49-199 across glut vs supply-short re-lease paths and ~$76-173 across capex and ERP; owned-site facility cost is now the largest single lever ($53 at $25M/MW facility, $151 at $12M).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Round 4 rebuilds the round-3 cohort DCF from the site inventory. Every inventory site enters once with its MW and timing: (1) ~650 MW revenue-earning at start-2027 = Vineland 300 MW (Microsoft) + 350 MW across the other energized sites and the late-2026 phases of Bethune, Beit Shemesh, Masmiya, Tallinn and Birmingham; inside the 350 MW, Meta's 2025 contract (~$0.58B/yr, ~48 MW, pro rata because its site is undisclosed) and the signed Q2-26 deals (>$4B, ~$1.6B/yr 2027-28) are carried as contracts; the rest bills at market/mid-term on the round-3 curve (2027 fleet revenue ~$8.45B, $13M/MW, unchanged). (2) Signed contracts at their terms: Microsoft $3.48B/yr 2027-30 plus 45% of 2031 (TCV $17.4B through 2031); Meta 2025 $0.58B/yr to 2030; Meta $12B dedicated on ~133 MW (Mantsala 2 + first Lappeenranta phase) at 1.2/2.4/2.4/2.4/2.4/1.2 $B in 2027-32; Meta's up-to-$15B backstop as a $18M/MW revenue floor for five years on ~167 MW of Birmingham clusters (revenue = max(market, floor)). (3) Uncontracted construction and pipeline probability-weighted (95% to 50%, see site_coverage), net of their own capex, on site dates (Highridge 260/660/1,000/1,200 MW by Oct-27/Jan-29/Nov-29/2030; Independence 150-250 MW a year 2027-31; Lappeenranta, Birmingham, Bethune remainder, UK, Madrid, AIB, Oklahoma): 3.45 GW named full build, ~2.8 GW expected. After 2031 capacity grows 3%/yr (unnamed future sites). (4) Owned vs leased costs (flag F2): owned MW pay power ($0.8M) + other fixed opex ($2.35M) per MW and capex $36.25M/MW ($20.25M GPU/servers + $16M facility) plus 2.5%/yr facility maintenance; leased MW pay the same plus colocation rent $2.35M/MW and capex $22M/MW (GPU + fit-out). Kept from round 3: new-vintage ACV $22/21/20M x 85% sold; 2-year mid-term contracts, 35% of capacity on 5-year terms in the long run (22% for uncontracted 2027-28 cohorts because Meta's clusters are now explicit); re-lease index 1.00/0.90/0.74/0.62/0.55/0.49/0.43/0.38; 6-year refresh at full GPU cost with 7% x 0.75 salvage; 12% variable opex; tax 25%; Gordon terminal (g 3%) on the 2040-45 average; net claims -$4.08B (cash $1.2B - secured $0.78B - deferred revenue $8B + stakes $3.5B); 380M shares; equity rolled to Oct-2027 at 13.6% (contracted PV at its own rate). Asset-light partner capacity adds $0.86B (30% x 300 MW x $1.5M/MW net fee). Output: revenue 2027 $12.6B, 2028 $27.3B, 2029 $39.9B; EV $44.9B single-rate (PV FCF $26.6B incl. asset-light $0.86B, TV $17.4B) -> $118/sh; split-rate EV $46.0B (IG contract FCF PV $4.93B at 8.5% vs $3.82B at WACC; unrated $1.31B vs $1.27B) -> $121/sh. Sensitivities (single / split, $/sh): life 4/5/6/7/8y 101/123/118/112/96 (split 103/126/121/115/99); glut path 47/50, supply-short 196/199; capex owned/leased $32.25/20 - $36.25/22 - $40.25/24 at WACC 11.6/12.3/12.9%: 170/150/134, 138/118/104, 105/87/73; all pipeline at 100% probability 139/142; post-2028 phases at 50% 110/113; contract rates 7.5%/10% 122 split, 9.5%/11% 120 split; long-run 5-year share 20%/50% 100/137; no Meta 2026 contracts 116 split; no salvage 108/111; owned facility $12M/$25M per MW 148/50.

inputs_detail.value: 650 MW at $13M/MW blended (2027 revenue $8.45B): Vineland 300 MW (Microsoft) + 350 MW other energized/late-2026 phases (FI-MAN1 75, US-KC 40, IS-KEF 10, FR-PAR 5, UK-LCX ~13, IL-MOD ~5, US-MN ~10, FR-BET 120, IL-MAS 22, IL-BSH 30, EE-TLL 10, US-BHM 10)
inputs_detail.derivation: Exit-2026 ARR guide $7-9B / $12M per MW = ~0.65 GW active (connected 0.8-1.0 GW is not active, flag F6); +8% for the Oct-1 list-price increases. Site split from the inventory: energized envelopes (~430 MW) plus the phases due before YE26 (Bethune ~half of 240 MW per Reuters, Masmiya Q3-26, Beit Shemesh phased Q3-26 to Q1-27, Tallinn first phase, Birmingham initial energization Q4-26). Undisclosed allocations (Longcross ~4,000-9,000 B300 = ~13 MW; Modi'in, Woodbury) are judgment. Non-contract part bills at a $17.1M/MW basis x 85% on a 2-year mid-term term, then the re-lease index; refreshed at age 6 (2032).

inputs_detail.value: $3.48B/yr 2027-2030, 45% of a year in 2031; then re-lease at m(6)=0.49 and refresh in 2031
inputs_detail.derivation: TCV $17.4B over five years through 2031 (6-K); tranches Nov-2025 to Aug-2026, so the term ends ~mid-2031 and ~$1.5B was billed in 2026. 300 MW is the Nebius figure (secondary 315/350 MW includes Phase 2, which I leave out as undisclosed); implies ~$11.6M/MW-yr. Microsoft pays Nebius; Nebius pays DataOne (build-to-suit landlord) via the leased-site colocation cost.

inputs_detail.value: ~$0.58B/yr 2027-2030 (+10% of 2031) on ~48 MW inside the energized fleet
inputs_detail.derivation: ~$2.9-3B over five years from Dec-2025/Feb-2026 deliveries (I use $2.9B, the 6-K figure, over the letter's rounded $3B). Site undisclosed, so the MW (~48 at ~$12M/MW) sit pro rata across the energized non-Vineland sites; no MW counted twice. Probable collateral for the $775M facility (inventory F12).

inputs_detail.value: ~133 MW (Mantsala 2 70 MW + Lappeenranta 63 MW) at ~$18M/MW; $1.2/2.4/2.4/2.4/2.4/1.2B in 2027-32; 95% completion probability
inputs_detail.derivation: Five years per order from early 2027 tranches on Vera Rubin; press names Finland/UK/US. I map it to the two Finnish owned builds due 2027 (judgment; the alternative US mapping changes little). ~$18M/MW is a hyperscaler discount to the $20-25M Q2-26 ACV; MW = $2.4B / $18M. Late-delivery fee discounts are the completion risk, captured by the 95% probability and the 8.5% rate.

inputs_detail.value: Revenue floor $18M/MW for 5 years on ~167 MW of Birmingham clusters (90 MW 2027, 77 MW 2028); revenue = max(market, floor); 90% probability
inputs_detail.derivation: Meta must buy unsold capacity on specified clusters for five years from each cluster's deployment (flag F3). $15B / 5 yrs / $18M = ~167 MW. Clusters are unspecified; I assign them to Birmingham's first owned phases (judgment). The floor binds from age 3 when the market path falls below $18M; worth ~+$2.5/sh in level and moves ~$15B of revenue into the contracted (8.5%) bucket.

Four deals averaging >$1B (Reflection AI, Cohere, a US neolab, a US quant firm), 1-3 year terms, $20-25M/MW; ~70% carry prepayments covering 50-60% of capex. Treated as part of the market-billed fleet (no extra MW), discounted at 10.5% for the contract term.

Dates from site pages and letters. Probability = completion x lease-up: owned sites with power and permits under construction 85-90% for first phases, 65-80% for 2029+ phases that need additional utility power (IPL 'additional power by early 2029') and ~$25-30B/yr of financing (Redburn's ~$200B gap); host-funded colocation under construction 90-95%; signed leases not yet built 85%; UK fourth site 75% (unnamed); Oklahoma 50% (no MW disclosed, 100 MW assumed, city conflicting). Expected MW and capex scale together, so each site is valued net of the capex needed to build it; financing enters through the WACC and the negative early FCF.

inputs_detail.value: Owned $36.25M ($20.25M GPU/servers + $16M facility) + 2.5%/yr facility maintenance; leased $22M ($20.25M + $1.75M fit-out); refresh $20.25M less 7% x 0.75 salvage
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3's $27M blended (75% GPU) was calibrated to the 1y10m payback on late-2026 capacity, which is mostly leased, so the GPU+fit-out part carries over as the leased figure. Owned facility: JLL shell-and-core ~$11.3M/MW in 2026 plus liquid-cooling plant $4.5-5.2M/MW = ~$16M (ClusterBid's $25-40M is the high case, shown as sensitivity). Check: colo rent $2.35M/MW-yr capitalised over 20 years at 12.3% is ~$17M, so owning is modestly cheaper, consistent with the company's owned-site strategy (Q1-26 letter).

inputs_detail.value: Owned $3.15M/MW (power $0.8M + other fixed $2.35M); leased $5.5M/MW (+ colocation $2.35M); + 12% of revenue
inputs_detail.derivation: Round-3 $5.5M split per the supervisor and flag F2: colocation ~$196/kW-month (~$2.35M/MW-yr) is charged only on leased/colocated MW; owned MW pay power (~$0.8M at 85% load, PUE ~1.2, ~$0.08/kWh) and the other fixed costs. Leases of 10-12 years (Harlow, AIB) are fixed costs charged on every leased MW through the terminal, whether or not rents decay (flag F9).

Unchanged approach. Company book lives per the fact-checked note: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 (from 1 Jan 2026), IREN 5, hyperscalers 5-6. Round 3 wrongly said IREN uses 6. The cash tail stays positive to ~age 8 even with the lower owned-site fixed cost; refilling scarce MW is worth slightly more at 5 years (+$5), but a capital-constrained Nebius is likelier to sweat assets, so 6 stays the base.

inputs_detail.value: $22/21/20M x 85% sold; 2-year mid-term; 5-year share 35% long run, 22% for uncontracted 2027-28 cohorts
inputs_detail.derivation: As round 3. Meta's ~300 MW of 2027-28 clusters (~17% of those cohorts) are now explicit, so the other 2027-28 cohorts carry (35-17)/83 = ~22% on unsigned 5-year terms; refresh cycles and 2029+ cohorts keep 35%.

inputs_detail.value: IG contract-term cash flows 8.5%; signed unrated 10.5%; everything else and terminal at WACC 12.3%
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchor: Nebius's secured facility against an IG contract at SOFR + 2.50% (SOFR 3.87%, i.e. 6.4% floating today); fixed-equivalent over the ~4-year average contract life is ~4.95% (3-5y Treasuries 4.91-5.01%) + 2.50% = ~7.45%. Plus ~100bp for the slice above the debt (lenders cover >100% of capex, not 100% of contract cash flow), Microsoft's termination right on missed delivery and Meta's late-delivery fee discounts gives 8.5%. Meta's own 2031 notes at 4.55% are the pure-credit floor. Unrated Q2-26 labs/quant firm: 10.5%, halfway to WACC because prepayments cover 50-60% of capex on ~70% of deals but the counterparties are venture-funded.

Unchanged: rf 5.29% (FRED 9/30; 5.24% on 10/1) + beta 1.8 x ERP 4.6% (Damodaran 4.14% to 5.0%); 85/15 equity/debt with debt at ~7% pre-tax. I do not lower the WACC on the residual even though the contracted cash flows are now taken out at 8.5%, which makes the split-rate figure generous (a pure residual rate would be ~12.8-13%).

inputs_detail.value: Asset-light 30% x 300 MW x $1.5M/MW-yr net fee from 2029, no capex, at WACC = $0.86B; Palantir $0
inputs_detail.derivation: Initial partner arrangements were signed Jul-2026 but no MW are disclosed, so this is a small probability-weighted option. Palantir modular deployments run on capacity at existing sites, so counting them would double-count MW; no commitment is disclosed.

Unchanged from round 3: cash ~$1.2B - $0.78B secured debt - ~$8B deferred revenue (prepaid revenue the DCF also counts) + $3.5B stakes; converts in the share count. Nebius's own AIB prepayment (Nebius pays the landlord) sits in the leased fit-out capex.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM EBITDA $12.1B (NTM revenue ~$22B x 55%) x 9x = EV $108.9B; less Oct-2027 net financial debt ~$2.5B, plus stakes $3.5B = $109.9B / 400M shares = $275.

inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged at ~$22B: between consensus (2027 $12.3B and growing) and the site-mapped DCF's probability-weighted NTM ~$23.6B (round 3: ~$27B); BNP's ~$22B exit-2027 ARR is the run-rate anchor.

Round 3 used 52% against a model at 51-54%. The site-mapped model gives ~61% NTM (2028 62%) because owned MW no longer pay colocation (flag F2) and Microsoft/Meta/Q2 contract revenue stays flat in 2028. I credit about half the gain because owned capacity only ramps through the NTM window; Nebius's AI cloud margin was 49.7% in Q2-26.

CoreWeave: EV $94.9B / forward sales ~$19.5B (P/S 2.5x on $48.9B cap) = ~4.9x sales; at ~60% margin = ~8x forward EBITDA (round 1 wrongly read 14.8x LTM as ~11x forward). 1x premium for Nebius's near-zero financial net debt (CoreWeave debt $51.6B, Altman Z 0.29) and faster growth; Redburn's Sell argues against more. GPU-life research does not change it: CoreWeave's multiple already prices a 6-year book life and the same re-contracting risk.
Unchanged at $2.5B: the site-mapped model's 2027 capex ($26.7B) is close to round 3's $27.0B (higher owned-site capex offset by probability weighting and Highridge's late-2027 start).
380M + ~$5B equity at ~$250 = ~20M shares.
As in DCF (supervisor haircut).

bear.story: GPU supply catches up (Rubin volume, more power): re-lease rents follow the glut path, mid-term contracts roll off at $10-12M/MW, new deals slide toward $17-20M/MW, the 2029+ Highridge/Independence phases slip for lack of power or financing, and owned facilities cost nearer ClusterBid's $25M/MW. The glut-path DCF is ~$47-65 (up from $17-41 in round 3 because Microsoft, the two Meta contracts and the backstop floor now carry ~$5B of PV at 8.5%); the market prices the stock near invested capital less claims.

base.story: Exit-2026 ARR ~$8B, 2027 revenue ~$13-14B, exit-2027 ARR ~$20-22B; Meta's dedicated tranches start on time in Finland and Birmingham clusters fill above the backstop floor; Highridge's first 260 MW arrives in late 2027; new deals hold ~$20-22M/MW; EBITDA margins mid-50s as owned capacity ramps; the multiple compresses toward CoreWeave's ~8-9x forward EBITDA, leaving the price a little below today.

bull.story: Compute stays sold out through 2027: expiring capacity re-books near original prices, short-term deals at >$40M/MW grow, new vintages price at $24M+/MW, all owned campuses run to schedule (pipeline at 100%: DCF ~$142) and the supply-short path gives a DCF ~$199; the multiple holds and the stock re-rates toward $399-415 targets.

thesis_break_reason: At $115 the equity is ~$44B on ~380M diluted shares, below the Sep-2025 conversion price ($138.75) and just under my site-mapped DCF at one WACC ($118; $121 split-rate). That DCF already probability-weights every uncontracted site and gives the signed Microsoft/Meta cash flows only ~$5B of PV, so trading there would most likely mean the market has stopped paying for Q2-26 deal economics or for the 2028-29 owned campuses: re-lease rents on the glut path (DCF ~$47-65), new-deal $/MW slipping below ~$20M, Highridge/Independence phases slipping for power or financing, or a Meta tranche delay, rather than ordinary 100%-vol noise.

Customer concentration (Meta ~$30B incl. backstop, Microsoft $17.4B, four >$1B Q2 deals) and AI-lab demand dependent on venture funding
reasoning: Round 4 does two things. (1) Site coverage: I rebuilt the cohort DCF from the checked inventory, so each of the 25 sites enters once with its MW, timing and owned/leased status. The ~650 MW revenue-earning fleet at start-2027 is mapped to Vineland (300 MW, Microsoft) and the other energized sites plus the late-2026 phases of Bethune, Israel, Tallinn and Birmingham. Signed contracts are cash flows at their terms: Microsoft $3.48B/yr to mid-2031, Meta 2025 $0.58B/yr to 2030, Meta's $12B dedicated on ~133 MW of Finnish builds from 2027, and Meta's up-to-$15B backstop as a five-year $18M/MW revenue floor on ~167 MW of Birmingham clusters (flag F3). Uncontracted builds and pipeline are probability-weighted (95% to 50%) on site dates, net of their own capex: 3.45 GW full build, ~2.8 GW expected. Flag F2 (facility cost counted twice on owned MW) is fixed. Owned MW now pay power and site opex but no colocation, and carry a realistic facility capex of $16M/MW (JLL shell-and-core plus liquid cooling) and 2.5%/yr maintenance. Leased MW keep colocation rent and lower capex. Bridge from $117: site schedule (3.45 GW named at later dates vs 4.3 GW generic adds) -$15; Meta now explicit, so other 2027-28 cohorts carry 22% on 5-year terms instead of 35%, -$5; Meta contracts and backstop +$3; probability weighting -$14; owned/leased cost split +$50; facility maintenance -$20; asset-light +$2.5. That gives $118 at one WACC. (2) Split discounting: IG contract-term cash flows at 8.5%, anchored on the SOFR+2.50% secured facility (fixed-equivalent ~7.45% at 3-5y Treasuries ~4.95%) plus ~100bp for delivery/termination risk and the unfinanced slice; signed unrated Q2-26 deals at 10.5%; everything else at 12.3%. The split adds only ~$3 ($118 -> $121). The signed contracts run just 4-5 years, and the contracted bucket includes the 2027 build capex of the Meta clusters, so the IG FCF PV rises only from $3.8B to $4.9B. Contract-rate sensitivity is small ($120-122). Most of the value sits in uncontracted re-lease and the terminal, at WACC. The EV/EBITDA leg rises to $275 (margin 52% -> 55%, crediting half of the model's higher owned-site margin). Blend $198 (from $188). I raise the base scenario to $215 and the bear case to $90: the contracted floor lifts the glut-path DCF from $17-41 to $47-65. The bull case stays at $400. P(>=spot) moves 0.424 -> 0.439. The thesis break stays at $115, now just under the single-rate DCF. I fixed one fact from the fact-check: IREN's life is 5 years, not 6. I also corrected the CoreWeave pricing quote in a source title. Research this round: one web search (owned data-center cost per MW) plus fetches of the NY Fed SOFR, the Treasury curve and ClusterBid. No option data or priors were used, and I did not open other forecasters' files.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Signed contracts at their terms (Microsoft to mid-2031, Meta 2025 to 2030, Meta $12B dedicated 2027-32, Meta backstop floor $18M/MW for five years on its clusters); other capacity at contract price for its term (2-year mid-term; 35% long-run on 5-year terms, 22% for uncontracted 2027-28 cohorts), then re-lease at 1.00/0.90/0.74/0.62/0.55/0.49/0.43/0.38 of the initial price at ages 1-8; cash margin over opex (owned $3.15M/MW, leased $5.5M/MW, + 12%) stays positive to ~age 8; refresh at age 6 at full GPU cost ($20.25M/MW) at the then-current new-vintage price, 7% salvage x 0.75.
gpu_life.note: Nebius self-operates its GPU cloud, so the research applies in full. Values are split-rate DCFs (single-rate 123/118/112). The value-maximizing life is 5 years ($126; 4y $103, 8y $99); I keep 6 as the base because a capital-constrained Nebius is likelier to sweat assets. Company lives per the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5 (round 3 wrongly gave IREN 6). The re-lease path matters more than the life: supply-short $199, glut $50. The owned-site cost fix lowers the tail's cash floor for owned MW (no colocation), which the supervisor asked for, but the optimum stays at 5-6 years.

discounting.basis: Rates in % a year. Investment-grade contract-term cash flows (Microsoft AAA to mid-2031; Meta AA-/Aa3: 2025 contract to 2030, $12B dedicated 2027-32, backstop floor for five years from each cluster) at 8.5%. Anchor: Nebius's $775M secured facility against an IG contract at SOFR + 2.50% (SOFR 3.87% on Oct 1 = ~6.4% floating; fixed-equivalent ~7.45% using 3-5y Treasuries at 4.91-5.01%), plus ~100bp for completion/operating risk (Microsoft can terminate for missed delivery; Meta gets fee discounts for late delivery) and the equity slice above the secured debt. Meta's 2031 notes at 4.55% are the pure-credit floor. Signed unrated Q2-26 deals (Reflection AI, Cohere, a neolab, a quant firm; 1-3 years, ~70% with prepayments covering 50-60% of capex) at 10.5%. Post-contract, unsigned (including assumed future 5-year deals), pipeline, asset-light and terminal cash flows at WACC 12.3%. Contracted buckets include the 2027-28 build capex of the Meta clusters, so the uplift is small: IG FCF PV $4.93B at 8.5% vs $3.82B at WACC, unrated $1.31B vs $1.27B. Equity is rolled to Oct-2027 with contracted PV accreting at its own rate. Sensitivity: 7.5%/10% gives $122, 9.5%/11% gives $120.
